definitions.explanation: The quality of a musical sound that distinguishes different instruments or voices playing the same pitch. Also used more broadly for the quality of any sound.

examples.japanese: ⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧⟦ピアノ→ピアノ：01376_piano⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{美|うつく}しい→美しい：01121_utsukushii⟧{音色|ねいろ}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: This piano has a beautiful tone.
I like the tone of her voice.

examples.japanese: ⟦バイオリン→バイオリン：00009_baiorin⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦チェロ→チェロ：08115_chero⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{音色|ねいろ}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{違|ちが}う→違う：01957_chigau⟧。
examples.english: The violin and cello have different timbres.

notes:
WRITING:
- {音|ね} - sound
- ⟦{色|いろ}→色：00849_iro⟧ - color

The compound literally means "color of sound," capturing how timbre is the "color" that makes each instrument unique.

PRONUNCIATION:
Also read as おんしょく in technical/academic contexts.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ⟦{美|うつく}しい→美しい：01121_utsukushii⟧{音色|ねいろ} - beautiful tone
- ⟦{独特|どくとく}→独特：01656_dokutoku⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{音色|ねいろ} - distinctive timbre
- ⟦{温|あたた}かい→温かい：13395_atatakai⟧{音色|ねいろ} - warm tone
- ⟦{澄|す}んだ→澄む：13370_sumu⟧{音色|ねいろ} - clear tone

MUSICAL CONTEXT:
{音色|ねいろ} is what allows us to distinguish:
- A violin from a flute playing the same note
- One singer from another
- Different piano brands

RELATED WORDS:
- ⟦{音程|おんてい}→音程：07109_ontei⟧ - pitch, musical interval
- ⟦{音量|おんりょう}→音量：10009_onryou⟧ - volume
- ⟦{音質|おんしつ}→音質：21879_onshitsu⟧ - sound quality

REGISTER:
Neutral. Common in music discussions and everyday conversation.
